cards.text: Nahum the prophet has a message for Nineveh, and here it comes: one who scatters is marching on the city. Friend, that is NOT who you want showing up on the doorbell camera. So Nahum calls out to Nineveh to guard the fortress, watch the road, brace up and summon all its strength.

cards.question: In the middle of all that, Nahum brings up Jacob, God's people. Destroyers laid them waste and ruined the branches of their vine. What will the LORD do for Jacob?

cards.text: The attackers roll in with red shields, warriors dressed in scarlet, and chariot fittings that flash like fire. Friend, my whole wardrobe is one white apron, and these folks showed up COLOR-COORDINATED.

cards.question: The chariots dash through the streets and rush around the plazas, darting about like lightning and appearing like ___.

cards.text: Someone summons his nobles, and they stumble as they advance, like me carrying a full tray to the oven. They race to the wall, and the protective shield is set in place.

cards.question: The river gates are thrown open, but the palace stands firm.
With the palace down, what is decreed for the city?

answers.text: That it be exiled and carried away
That it pay a yearly tribute
That it be rebuilt in stone

cards.text: Oh, friend. Listen to that: her maidservants moan like doves and beat upon their breasts, and I bet that's a sound nobody in that city ever forgets.
Then Nahum paints a picture: all her days, Nineveh has been like a pool of water. Friend, my apron has been clean all its days too, and we ALL know how long that lasts around chocolate chips.

cards.question: Nineveh has been like a pool of water all her days. What is happening to that pool now?
As the pool drains, the cry goes out, "Stop! Stop!" and no one turns back.

cards.text: Then a new shout goes up: "Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold!" Friend, that's not a battle cry anymore. That's the office group chat when somebody types "free stuff in the break room."

cards.question: As Nineveh's silver and gold are plundered, Nahum says the treasure soon runs out.
After the plundering, how does Nahum describe Nineveh?
As Nineveh is emptied, Nahum says knees knock and every face grows pale.

cards.text: Then Nahum asks where the lions' lair is now, the feeding ground where the lion and lioness prowled with nothing to frighten them away. Friend, NOTHING scared them, and a dropped baking sheet sends me three feet in the air, gold base and all.

cards.question: In Nahum's picture, the lion mauled enough for its ___ and filled its lairs with mauled ___.
Then the LORD of Hosts speaks. He tells Nineveh that He is ___ her.

cards.text: And He spells it out: chariots to cinders, the sword devours the young lions, and the prey gets cut off from the earth. Friend, the last time I saw cinders I'd left a batch in during a phone call, and even THAT wasn't this final.

cards.question: One more thing the LORD says will be gone. What will no longer be heard?

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the plunder shout, the line about it no longer being a battle cry, and the office-group-chat punchline. Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The distractors “straw” and “stones” create the nonsensical completions “mauled straw” and “mauled stones.” They are not believable alternatives for the lion's actions and make the correct answers stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
